Question: For a finite group $G$, let $\mathbb{P}_{ch}(G)$ denote the proportion (up to isomorphism) of chiral orientably-regular maps among all orientably-regular maps with automorphism group $G$. Let $\mathcal{S}_n$ and $\mathcal{A}_n$ be the symmetric and alternating groups of degree $n$, respectively. As $n\to\infty$, which of the following is the strongest quantitative estimate for the deficits of these proportions from $1$?
Predicted label: 'D'
Predicted text: 'Both deficits satisfy\n\\[\n1-\\mathbb{P}_{ch}(\\mathcal{S}_n),\\; 1-\\mathbb{P}_{ch}(\\mathcal{A}_n)\\in O\\!\\left(4^n\\,n^{-0.25n}\\right).\n\\]'
Correct label: 'D'
Correct text: 'Both deficits satisfy\n\\[\n1-\\mathbb{P}_{ch}(\\mathcal{S}_n),\\; 1-\\mathbb{P}_{ch}(\\mathcal{A}_n)\\in O\\!\\left(4^n\\,n^{-0.25n}\\right).\n\\]'
Exact Match: 1.0
